answer: Agents earn access to a harbor’s shared market only after completing a sequence of small tasks whose rewards are locked for weeks and forfeited if the same economic stake backs multiple identities. A haven of independent task issuers makes collusion harder: each checks different work, while a cipher-linked commitment lets them detect reused stakes without exposing every account publicly. A sybil attacker must therefore fund many distinct stakes, keep them locked, and produce credible work across issuers, making fake identities costly rather than free.
